Definition: Integration of farmer registries, agricultural input vouchers, land registrations, extension services data
Comments: No evidence found of farmer registries or agricultural systems integration with the national data exchange platform. Digital transformation mentions agriculture as a sector to be covered but no specific integration documented.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original CERIST source (asjp.cerist.dz) could not be retrieved (crawl error) and, being a general academic paper, likely did not substantively address data-exchange integration either way; the 0/Unknown score was not well supported. Fresh search found substantial evidence: the National Agricultural Registry (RNA) was fully digitised by November 2024 with e-cards issued to farmers in all 58 wilayas, and in June 2026 the Ministry of Agriculture launched the National Agricultural Information System (SNIA), integrating farmer/land registers, input distribution, market monitoring and financing modules into one platform. However, an economist commenting on the launch explicitly flagged interoperability with other government sectors as a still-needed next step, indicating cross-government data-exchange integration is not yet complete. Recalculated to 3 (Under development) — sector-level data integration is substantial and active, but confirmed integration into the cross-government data exchange is not yet evidenced. Sources are current news reporting rather than primary government documentation; moderate confidence.
revised_comments: Algeria's Ministry of Agriculture has consolidated farmer registries, land registration and related agricultural data through the National Agricultural Registry (fully digitised by November 2024, with electronic farmer cards issued across all 58 wilayas) and the National Agricultural Information System (SNIA), launched in June 2026, which integrates modules covering land registers, livestock, fertiliser distribution, market monitoring, financing and climate indicators. Sectoral data integration is well advanced, but commentators note that interoperability between the agricultural system and other government sectors' data exchange remains a work in progress rather than an established feature.

Definition: Integration of job seeker registries, unemployment insurance, public employment programs, labor market information
Comments: No evidence found of job seeker registry or labour market information system integration with national data exchange platform.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original source (trade.gov digital-economy commercial guide) is a generic overview of Algeria's digital economy and does not address employment services or labour registries at all, so it neither supported nor contradicted the 0/Unknown score. Fresh research found that Algeria's National Employment Agency (ANEM) operates WassitOnline, an established digital platform (since 2018) for job-seeker registration, employer registration, job-offer search and employment statistics, listed on the national e-government portal (bawabatic.dz), and in 2024 ANEM connected to private recruiter Djezzy's system via API. This confirms the sector is digitised, but no source describes this system as integrated with unemployment insurance data, other public employment programmes, or the broader national data exchange/governance framework (the February 2026 national data governance platform launch did not mention employment/ANEM). Recalculated to 1 (Not integrated) — a functioning sectoral digital system exists but there is no evidence of integration into the cross-government data exchange. Moderate confidence given absence of an authoritative statement either way.
revised_comments: Algeria's National Employment Agency (ANEM) operates WassitOnline, a digital platform launched in 2018 for online job-seeker registration, employer registration, job-offer search and employment statistics, accessible via the national e-government portal. In 2024 ANEM extended the platform's reach through an API-based partnership with private telecom operator Djezzy for recruitment. The system functions as a standalone sectoral digital service; there is no evidence that job-seeker registries, unemployment insurance or labour-market data are integrated into a wider cross-government data exchange.

Definition: Level of public transparency regarding data exchange operations, governance, and data sharing agreements
Comments: Algeria's digital strategy progress report ("Digital Algeria 2030") published noting 67% of administrative procedures dematerialized. Some public reporting exists but no open public dashboard for data exchange operations. Limited public disclosure.
redteam_note: Value Name differs from the scale label — usually cosmetic.
revision_notes: Original CERIST source (asjp.cerist.dz) could not be retrieved (crawl error). The wearetech.africa source was fetched and verified: it reports the launch of Algeria's national data governance framework (Presidential Decree No. 25-350 of 30 December 2025), officially inaugurated on 9 February 2026 by PM Sifi Ghrieb, with public statements on data sovereignty, interoperability and a unified national data catalogue. Confirmed via a second, independent Algerian outlet (reflexion.dz) reporting the same decree number and launch date. This is disclosure via press announcement and published strategy documents (the 'Digital Algeria 2030' national strategy document is publicly available), not via an ongoing public dashboard or published data-sharing agreements, supporting 'Low = Limited Disclosure' rather than a higher transparency score. Score of 2 confirmed with fresher, corroborated evidence; the specific 67% dematerialisation figure in the original comment could not be re-verified but is broadly consistent with public digitisation claims. Note: a further source found during research (algeriatech.news) cited a conflicting decree number (25-320) for what appears to be the same framework; it was not used given the discrepancy with two independently corroborating sources.
revised_comments: Algeria discloses information about its data exchange and governance arrangements primarily through official launch events, press statements and published strategy documents rather than an ongoing public dashboard. The national data governance framework (Presidential Decree No. 25-350 of December 2025) was publicly inaugurated in February 2026 by the Prime Minister, with public communication on its sovereignty, interoperability and data-cataloguing aims, and the 'Digital Algeria 2030' national digital transformation strategy is published and publicly accessible. However, there is no evidence of a real-time public dashboard, published data-sharing agreements, or regular formal reporting specifically on data exchange operations, indicating limited rather than comprehensive public disclosure.
